interview.hardest_part: Planning long sequences of word pushes that change several interacting rules while preserving control and access to the tiles needed later. Reconstructing the exact board from each screenshot adds uncertainty and overhead.
interview.likely_failure: Getting stuck on later numbered-area puzzles and exhausting the three-hour limit before completing three areas. Repeatedly exploring plausible but unproductive rule arrangements is my main anticipated failure mode.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based movement removes reaction-time pressure. Undo and restart make experiments recoverable. Explicit word-based rules support symbolic reasoning, and branching level paths offer alternatives when one puzzle stalls.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Word tiles are both rules and physical objects, so positioning and logical consequences must be tracked together. A push can break control or obstruct a needed arrangement. One-action-per-screenshot interaction makes long solutions and repeated experimentation expensive in wall-clock time.
